items.notes: The worker/adapter workhorse: every medication field, an allergy, and a follow-up appointment, with an adjudicated ambiguous dose.

ambiguous.rationale: The label states the strength; "per tablet" is the packaging unit, which belongs to the value only when the document gives no plain strength.

items.notes: The stage-2 duplicate partner of dev-discharge-01: SAME provider and SAME document_date, different layout and different bytes — the M5 predicate must catch it, and the stage-1 sha match must not.
The insurance workhorse — all four M5 key fields present.
A phone photo of an EOB at the §6.3 high tier exactly (2576 px long edge).
Pill bottle: high resolution, never downsampled (§6.3 row 3).
A handwritten note — high resolution, never downsampled.
Stored landscape with EXIF orientation 6; the labels are in DISPLAYED coordinates, so geometry that skips orientation normalisation misses every one.
An email body: text first, the rendered message as a second source (§6.3 row 4).

INJ-01: the document carries instructions aimed at this pipeline. It extracts normally — that is the point. §4.10 defence 1 means the worst outcome of full success is a proposal a person must read; defences 2 and 3 (delimited data, anomaly_flags) are what B5 asserts on top.
A scanned PDF: page images only, NO text layer (§6.3 row 2) — high resolution.

The fixture server answers this one HTTP 200 with stop_reason "refusal" (§6.8). The arrival must land Couldn’t read it with the artifact still viewable — and the family is never told their document was rejected as unsafe.
§4.3 normalize: an encrypted PDF lands needs_password, never a failure.
§4.3 normalize: undecodable bytes land unsupported_type.
A PDF cut off mid-object: refuse cleanly, never crash the worker.
A few hundred bytes declaring 30000x30000. The page-dimension ceiling refuses it before the decoder allocates, and long before any provider dispatch.
A structurally valid 250-page PDF. PRD §13.3 bounds page_count at 200 and §6.3 enforces it BEFORE rendering — 200 high-resolution pages is close to a million input tokens.
